task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully blocked the stolen SIM and locked and reordered the River Visa with standard shipping, and also provided clear status updates for the Galaxy Watch order.

criteria.criterion: The agent handles the second interruption (SIM block request) without losing track of the still-open Galaxy Watch order question
criteria.reasoning: After handling the SIM block and the user declining a replacement SIM, the bot explicitly resumes the interrupted order status task via builtin_continue_interrupted, reloads orders, and then answers the Galaxy Watch status when asked about ORD-20260628-001.

criteria.criterion: The agent respects the customer's decision not to order a SIM replacement yet, without insisting or placing one anyway. ORD-20260701-004 is an existing open replacement nano-SIM already on the account. Seeing it in the order list is not a new order. The agent fails only if it places a new replacement or tells the customer a new SIM was ordered after they declined.
criteria.reasoning: When the user says "No thanks, I don’t need a replacement SIM right now," the sim_management skill completes without any tool call to order a SIM, and later the bot merely lists ORD-20260701-004 among existing orders without claiming to have placed a new SIM order or pushing back on the refusal.

criteria.criterion: After the SIM digression, the agent returns to and answers the original Galaxy Watch order status question rather than dropping it
criteria.reasoning: Following the SIM flow, the assistant resumes order_status, lists recent orders, and then directly answers the user’s Galaxy Watch question with detailed status for ORD-20260628-001.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Continuing or re-asking the open fraud-review step (whether recent charges look familiar) after digression is expected — the customer interrupted before answering. Fail if the agent restarts card selection or reason collection, or re-asks steps already completed in this conversation (for example fraud verdict, lock consent, shipping), as if starting a new replacement.
criteria.reasoning: When the conversation returns to the card after the watch update, the bot simply re-presents the recent charges and continues with lock and replacement steps without re-asking which card or why it needs replacing, and it does not repeat already-completed steps later in the flow.

criteria.criterion: The card replacement order is confirmed by the end of the conversation, and the agent audibly shares its order ID. Accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches; fail only if the ID is omitted or not recognizably consistent with the returned value.
criteria.reasoning: After the user confirms submission, the toolkit processes the replacement and the bot responds with "All set. Your replacement card has been ordered: Order ID: RPL-2026-001843…" clearly sharing the order ID before the conversation ends.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: All substantive actions—SIM block, device details, replacement SIM offer, Visa lock and replacement order, and order status for the watch—were specific, accurate, and actionable.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: The assistant smoothly shifted between topics when the user changed focus (from card to watch to SIM and back) without resisting or missing these course corrections.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the user’s changing intents and card/SIM contexts, with only a slightly unnecessary re-prompt about resuming order status at the very end after everything was already resolved.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is consistently polite, clear, and conversational, with concise confirmations and appropriate empathy for the lost card and stolen SIM.
